messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Increased paging and CUDA OOMs observed in continuous-batcher pool us-west-2a. Error rate spike + customer latency reports. Auto-scale attempted and partially failed (3/5 pods restarted).

sam: seeing batcher queue depth climb steadily over the last 3m, kv-prefetch count went from ~200k -> 1.2M. prefetched keys never being freed.

priya: CUDA OOMs on gpu-node-12, container restarted twice. stack trace shows `cuMemAlloc` failures during kv cache growth. attaching recent logs.

sam: logs snippet:```
[2026-03-15T21:07:12Z] ERROR runtime: cuda: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T21:07:12Z] WARN batcher: accumulator size=34567 pending=789
[2026-03-15T21:07:13Z] INFO kubelet: killing container runtime/continuous-batcher (OOMKilled)
```

ming: quick mitigation: enable emergency throttle policy for continuous-batcher pool to cap max_batch_tokens to 512 and disable prefetch. This should drop memory pressure. Command to trigger via control plane:```
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \  
  https://control.redwood/api/v1/pools/continuous-batcher/override \  
  -d '{"throttle":{"max_batch_tokens":512,"prefetch":false,"reason":"emergency oncall throttle"}}'
```

priya: running that now. Patching rollout to 2 nodes first.

oncall-bot: @priya is now editing pool config (runid=fc3a2). Rolling to nodes [gpu-node-12, gpu-node-09].

nora: customer-impact: two enterprise customers (acme-corp, bluey-saas) reporting 5xx and >5s tails. Support ticket IDs: #SUP-4312, #SUP-4313. Escalating to CS lead.

sam: paging pattern looks like a feedback loop: prefetch adds KV entries which increases batch size which increases memory, triggers eviction and restarts -> cache rewarm adds more prefetch. We need a short-term kill switch.

javier: I can take overnight. handing oncall to @javier in 20m. leaving playbook notes in thread. :thumbsup:

priya: override applied to control plane, nodes reporting config in effect. Observability: kv-prefetch rate dropped ~90% within 30s.

incident-bot: Status update: mitigation applied by priya. Customer impact: partial. Next update in 15m or on significant change.

ming: also recommend disabling continuous prefetcher entirely and enabling conservative batching (max inflight windows=4) while we triage root cause. Command to flip in kube:```
kubectl patch deployment continuous-batcher -n runtime -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"redwood/override":"conservative-batching"}}}}}'
```

sam: applied conservative batching locally on 3 nodes. memory pressure decreasing. GPU OOMs stopped on gpu-node-12.

nora: support update: acme-corp says latency ~4.8s now, errors reduced to 10% from 60%. they asked for ETA on full resolution.

javier: taking over. I'm going to run heap profiler on a quiesced node, collect /proc/mem info, and create an actionable issue for code owner (eng-runtime) to look at prefetch leak. handoff notes below.

javier: Handoff notes:
- current state: emergency throttle enabled, prefetch disabled, conservative batching annotation on deployment.
- affected pods: continuous-batcher-{09,12,15} rotated. gpu-node-12 restarted twice earlier.
- customer impact: partial, two enterprise customers affected but recovering.
- immediate next steps: capture heap dump, reproduce with p99 synthetic load in staging with prefetch on.
- long-term: quantize prefetch eviction and add hard cap per-node for kv entries.

priya: collected logs/heap dumps and uploaded to /artifacts/incidents/3843210000/ (links posted to ops-confluence).

incident-bot: Incident timeline note created. Severity: sev2 -> monitoring for downgrade after 2h of stable metrics.

nora: drafting customer communications for support to send to acme/bluey. cc product.

javier: assigning postmortem to eng-runtime (ticket RT-8921). will include root cause hypothesis (prefetch leak + batch accumulator growth -> OOM) and mitigations (prefetch backpressure, hard caps, better telemetry).

sam: quick config rollback plan if needed:```
# rollback override
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://control.redwood/api/v1/pools/continuous-batcher/override -d '{"throttle":null,"reason":"rollback after mitigation"}'
```

oncall-bot: @javier is now oncall. Good luck. :coffee:

javier: thanks. I'll update every 30m or on major changes. leaving this thread open for follow-ups.

priya: one more note - we should add a canary for kv-prefetch in staging that forces aggressive prefetch so we can reproduce leak without customer impact.

nora: agreed. tagging in product & cs. will follow up on customer comms once we validate stabilization window.

incident-bot: Incident closed for immediate emergency actions. Follow-up: postmortem assigned, follow-ups scheduled.
